title: What happens during a skin examination?
intro: A skin examination is a check of the skin for changes such as unusual moles, spots or rashes. It is used to detect skin cancer early and to diagnose skin conditions. It is quick and painless, and can be done by a family doctor or a dermatologist.

sections.heading: Why it is done
paragraphs: Skin cancer, including melanoma, is more treatable when found early. Doctors examine the skin for new or changing marks, assess rashes, and monitor existing conditions. People with many moles, fair skin, past sunburn, a family history of melanoma or a weak immune system benefit from regular checks.

sections.heading: How the examination is done
paragraphs: You undress to underwear and the doctor inspects the skin from head to toe, including the scalp, between the toes, nails and genital area if needed, with your consent. A hand-held magnifier called a dermatoscope shows structures within moles. Photographs may be taken to track changes.

sections.heading: What doctors look for
paragraphs: They look at asymmetry, irregular borders, uneven colour, a diameter larger than six millimetres and evolution, meaning change over time. Moles that itch, bleed or grow, and sores that do not heal, are also concerning. Most spots are harmless.

sections.heading: After the examination
paragraphs: If something looks suspicious, a small sample or the whole spot may be removed under local anaesthetic and examined. Results take days. You will be advised on checking your own skin and protecting it from the sun. Ask how often check-ups are advisable.

sections.heading: Checking your own skin
paragraphs: Look over your skin regularly in good light, using a mirror for the back. Note new spots or changes, and take photos to compare. Use shade, clothing, hats and sunscreen, and avoid sunbeds. See a doctor promptly about any mole that changes.

examples.title: Regular self-check
examples.text: Imagine you want to monitor your moles. You could photograph them every few months and show changes to your doctor.

examples.title: Reporting a change
examples.text: Suppose a mole has grown and itches. You might make an appointment soon and ask for a dermatoscopic examination.
